newsitem.title: UK: Ecuador c.bank sees 1997 growth at 3.6% - official.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador c.bank sees 1997 growth at 3.6% - official.

text.p: The Central Bank of Ecuador estimates 1997 gross domestic product growth will be 3.6 percent, Mauricio Valencia, the central bank's technical director, said on Wednesday.
Valencia, speaking at an investor presentation here, said 1998 growth was expected to be 4.0 percent.

In mid-May, Ecuador's central bank issued a statement that 1997 growth was forecast to be 3.3 percent, against a previous forecast of 3.5 percent. It also then said 1998 growth would be 4.3 percent against a prior forecast of 4.0.

Mauricio Pareja, another technical official at the central bank, also said at the presentation that Ecuador's objective was to reduce its budget deficit to 2.5 percent of GDP in 1997, and 1.3 percent of GDP in 1998.
Paraja also said Ecuador wanted to cut inflation in 1997 to 30 percent, and to 23 percent in 1998.
The forecasts were also contained in presentation documents given to delegates. The officials were in London to encourage private investment in Ecuador.
They said they were meeting with the Paris Club on Thursday over restructuring and refinancing of Ecuador's debt.
Pareja said the meeting would be to "normalise" relations with the Paris Club.
